title: In Evangelium Matthaei Commentarius
author: Hilary

passages.original: Ergo non occulta domus, sed cordis nostri ctibiculum ingredi, et clauso mentis nostræ secreto orare ad Deum, non multiloquio, sed conscienlia admonemur, quia dictorum verbis opus omne pnccellal. (a) De orationis autem sacramenlo necessitate nos commentandi Cyprianus vir sanctæ memoriæ liberavit. Quamquam et Tertullianus hinc volumen aptissimum scripserit: sed consequens error hominis, detraxit scriptis probabilibus auctoritatem.
passages.english: Therefore we are admonished to enter not a hidden [room of the] house but the inner chamber of our heart, and, with the secret place of our mind shut, to pray to God not with much speaking but with [our] conscience, because the deed surpasses every word that is spoken. (a) But Cyprian, a man of holy memory, has freed us from the need to comment on the sacrament of prayer. And yet Tertullian too wrote a most fitting volume on this; but the error of the man that followed took away authority from [his] commendable writings.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'ctibiculum' read as 'cubiculum', 'conscienlia' as 'conscientia', 'pnccellal' as 'praecellat' ("surpasses"), 'sacramenlo' as 'sacramento'. '(a)' is an editorial footnote mark. 'Opus omne' could also mean "every work [of devotion]". 'Sacramentum' may here mean "mystery" rather than "sacrament". The 'error' of Tertullian is presumably his later adherence to Montanism, but the text does not say so.
